text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
Pioneer colonial surgeon WILLIAM BLAND, who was transported for killing a fellow naval officer in a duel, was born in 1789.
New South Wales politician BENJAMIN LEE was born in 1825. He won his seat by giving away free alcohol to voters and he later became the first MP to punch another on the nose in Parliament House.

"King of the Cowboys" ROY ROGERS, who amassed a 100 million dollar fortune for various roles as singing cowboys, was born in 1912. His real name was LEONARD FRANKLIN SLYE and he appeared in his first film "Rhythm on the Range" in 1936. His first hit was in 1938 with "Hi-Yo Silver". During his career ROY made more than 91 films and more than 100 half-hourly western shows. In most films his horse "Trigger" was his co-star and when the horse died he was stuffed and displayed in the ROY ROGERS Museum.
British actress VIVIEN LEIGH, probably best known for her Oscar-winning role of Scarlett O'Hara in "Gone With The Wind", was born in 1913.

United States pianist, guitarist, singer, songwriter, talent scout and producer IKE TURNER was born in 1931. TURNER became one of the top session guitarists and in the fifties be produced B.B. KING among others. In 1956 he discovered ANNIE MAE BULLOCK in the audience and two years later married her. The couple performed as IKE and TINA TURNER. They were divorced in 1976 and TINA went on to a successful solo career. IKE was sentenced to a year in prison in 1988 for possession of and trafficking in drugs.
German actress ELKE SOMMER, who starred in "A Shot In The Dark" and "The Prize", was born in 1940.

American singer ART GARFUNKEL, who teamed with PAUL SIMON from as early as 1957, was born in 1942. ART worked as a solo artist from the seventies. His hits included "I Only Have Eyes For You" (1975), "What A Wonderful World" (1978) with JAMES TAYLOR and PAUL SIMON, and "Bright Eyes" (1979).

Canadian singer, guitarist and songwriter BRYAN ADAMS was born in 1959. His hits include "Straight From The Heart" (1983), "Run To You" (1984), "Heaven" (1985), "Summer Of '69" (1985), "Heat Of The Night" (1987) and "Everything I Do (I Do It For You)" (1991).
** EVENTS **
1605 : The so-called Gunpowder Plot was foiled when GUY

FAWKES was caught beneath the House of Lords in London with a tinder box and three matches. He intended to light the fuse to 36 barrels of gundpowder, secretly placed in the vault, and replace JAMES I and the assembled parliament with a Catholic monarchy.
1912 : The British Board of Film Censors was appointed.
1919 : The great screen lover RUDOLPH VALENTINO married
actress JEAN ACKER and was reportedly locked out on his wedding night.
1922 : HOWARD CARTER discovered the tomb of Tutankhamun
in the Valley of the Kings near Luxor in Egypt.
1924 : The last Manchu emperor, 18-year-old PU-YI, was
forced to leave his Peking palace by Christian warlord FENG YU-HSIANG, who took control of the city.
1938 : BENNY GOODMAN played MOZART with the Budapest
String Quartet.
1952 : Australian newspaperman Sir KEITH MURDOCH died at

the age of 67. He was chairman of Directors of the Herald and Weekly Times Ltd Melbourne and also controlling shareholder of Queensland Newspapers and News Limited Adelaide. He was survived by Lady MURDOCH, a son, RUPERT, and three daughters.
1956 : Soviet tanks crushed the Hungarian revolt.
1967 : The first roll-on, roll-off New Zealand ship the
"Hawea" arrived in Auckland.
1971 : Princess ANNE was named Sportswoman of the Year by
the British Sportswriters Association. The 21-year-old princess had become an accomplished all-round horse rider. She had just won the European Championships.
1987 : Sydney businessman ABE SAFFRON appealed after
bring sentenced to three years jail for tax fraud. The appeal was dismissed.
1991 : British embattled press baron ROBERT MAXWELL

drowned after mysteriously falling from his yacht off the Canary Islands. He wasn't missed for several hours and after an air and sea search his naked body was found. MAXWELL's death came after rumours about his health and the financial state of his business and his possible involvement with Mossad, the Israeli Secret Service. His death was also subject to rumour of suicide or murder. MAXWELL's media empire included the London Mirror group and the New York "Daily News".
1994 : "Muriel's Wedding" was voted best film at the
Australian Film Industry awards in Melbourne.
1994 : Sydney's controversial third runway began
operations, aimed at relieving delays at the airport. The runway has been subject of massive protests by Sydney residents.
